newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on harvest prospects.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on harvest prospects.

text.p: Prospects for a resumption soon in wheat harvesting in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region and persistent satisfactory weather for the soft red winter wheat crop pressured CBOT soft red winter wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
Wet weather slowed combining this week and storms overnight led to early concern about damage to a small portion of the crop in southern Kansas.
But analysts said the heavy rains could lead to a reduction in wheat quality localized areas of southern Kansas and probably would not affect the yields very much.

"We had a lot of rain in Wichita last night--up to four inches and that's going to cause delays. Test weights have been good but this delay is going to take them down some," said Sid Love, analyst for Joe Kropf and Sid Love Consulting.
The market also was pressured by spillover from Thursday's bearish USDA winter wheat production report.
USDA Thursday said 1997 U.S. winter wheat production would total 1.604 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimate for 1.579 billion.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 1/2 to eight cents per bushel lower, with July down 1/2 at $3.52-1/2.
Wheat was underpinned in early dealings by gains in soybean futures but when beans fell from the day's highs the strength in wheat quickly subsided.
Cargill Inc sold one million bushels of July, Merrill Lynch Futures bought two million bushels of September and Smith Barney bought one million bushels each of September and December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 24,000 contracts, below the 25,798 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 800 September $3.60 calls at 17-1/2 cents, Refco Inc sold 500 July $3.40 puts at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 cents, Smith Barney sold 500 July $3.30 puts at 1/2 cent and Paine Webber bought 500 September $5.20 calls at 5/8 cent, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000 contracts, below the 8,504 traded Thursday.
